factorRatings.note: Reviews describe sourdough-fermented, Neapolitan-style pies baked in a wood-fired dome oven with leopard-spotted crusts and a tangy, fermented crumb, alongside a standout rigatoni and house-made ice cream; The Infatuation includes it among the city's best pizza and best ice cream.

The Infatuation rates Moto's thick Detroit-style pies, made with a 100-year-old sourdough starter, an 8.4, praising crispy pepperoni edges and inventive toppings like Filipino pork belly; Seattle Refined reports online pre-orders have sold out months in advance.

The Infatuation calls the citywide chain (first opened on the Ave in 1979) 'a classic for a reason' at 7.6, good for a dependable slice or margherita; a 1996 Seattle Times review praised the original shop's springy, chewy crust and inventive 'Primo' toppings as probably the best pizza in Seattle at the time.

A Daily Hive feature on this Alki Italian restaurant calls its broad pizza menu (25-plus options, including BBQ chicken and Greek pies) flavor-packed with generous portions, reading as a casual neighborhood pasta-and-pizza spot rather than a pizza specialist.

The Infatuation rates this downtown slice counter 8.1, highlighting a charred, chewy crust and a distinctive shake of granulated garlic the reviewer says they haven't found at any other Seattle slice shop.

The Infatuation (7.5) singles out the prosciutto-and-egg and chicken pesto pies at this White Center counter; a Seattle Times feature on its pepperoni slice calls it a neighborhood staple since 2009 and notes Mashed named it the best pizza in Washington state.

The Infatuation rates this Belltown cocktail bar's New York-style pizza a 6.8 ('It's Fine'), citing inconsistent slice quality and an oregano-heavy red sauce, recommending it instead for drinks and a late-night bite.
